_doc: The one list of coding CLIs Allternit supports. Read by gizzi (src/runtime/providers/discovery/subprocess.ts — its subprocess brains) and embedded by allternit-api (src/cli_catalog.rs — CLI provider rows, sign-in, GET /api/v1/cli-tools/catalog). adapter: builtin = a protocol adapter in local-cli-driver.ts CLI_ADAPTERS; text = one-shot argv from headless.args ({prompt} is exactly one argv element, never a shell string; {model} from headless.modelArgs); unsupported = listed, not runnable as a brain yet. install.harness = the Factory installs it (pin + licence in factory/pane/src/ao/harness/harness.json); otherwise method npm|uv|brew|script with the pin verified against the registry on the date in _verified. Logos are paths in the web app's public dir. Version 2 adds model order and defaults as data: the order of a tool's models[] is the vendor's order (best/newest first) and is meaningful; a model with default: true is the tool's default model (at most one per tool; a tool whose only model is the placeholder "default" needs none, otherwise the first model is the default); defaultRank (lower = preferred) ranks the tools that may be picked automatically as the default CLI brain, mirroring Desktop's CLI_DEFAULT_ORDER (allternit-ai src/lib/default-brain.ts) - a tool without it is never an automatic default; liveModels {args, parser: codex-json|tsv|grok|ollama} is the command that prints the CLI's own model list, and models[] is the fallback when it fails; retired maps an old model id to its current id so saved choices keep working. Version 3 adds runtimes[]: the one list of runtimes a bot can run on (see CONTRACT-harness-bots-2.md). A runtime points to a tool with tool (null for allternit); adapter.kind says how it is driven; brains is "any" or a list of provider ids; look holds data-only terminal/desktop tokens; liveUi is the runtime's own web app. Run script/check-runtime-registry.ts after editing.
_verified: 2026-10-19 (npm registry, PyPI, formulae.brew.sh, vendor CLI docs)
